citation.title: Neural network-based analysis of charge exchange spectra in KSTAR
citation.authors: J.K. Lee, W.H. Ko, H.H. Lee, B. Kim, Y.H. Lee, G.W. Shin, J. Kim, J.M. Lee

scope_read.limitations: Figure values were read visually. CES frame exposure time, the campaign year of #28275, the hyperparameter values and the per-channel R² numbers are not tabulated.

claim_checks.proposed_claim: NN-CES maps a single raw spectrum to Doppler shift and width (giving C6+ Ti and toroidal rotation), trained on conventional beam-modulation labels.
claim_checks.source_finding: Per-channel MLP: 256-point raw spectrum normalized by its frame maximum, two hidden layers of 256 units, outputs Δλ and W_D, converted to Ti and vT. Loss combines MSE against modulation-analysis targets with a Gaussian-shape term against the target spectrum. Background estimation interpolates between preceding and succeeding beam-off intervals (1 Hz, 10 ms off).
claim_checks.locator: p1 Sec.1; p2 Sec.2.2 Eq.3; p3 Sec.3.1, Eqs.4-7; p4 Fig.3
claim_checks.allowed_intro_sentence: In KSTAR, a per-chord neural network has been trained on conventional beam-modulation analyses to read carbon CX Doppler shift and width directly from raw beam-on spectra, removing the need for beam-off background frames during inference [Lee2026].
claim_checks.qualification: The labels are conventional analysis outputs, not independent truth. The model predicts the current frame only.

claim_checks.proposed_claim: Agreement with modulation analysis declines toward the edge, around R ≳ 2.2 m.
claim_checks.source_finding: On held-out test-set R², shift is near 1 and width is about 0.9 inside about 2.2 m. Beyond that, the shift R² falls to about 0.2-0.3 and the width R² to about 0.4. The authors attribute this to a low active-to-passive signal ratio, ELMs and beam-on/off mismatch.
claim_checks.allowed_intro_sentence: Its agreement with the modulation analysis is high inside R≈2.2 m and degrades toward the edge, where passive emission dominates [Lee2026].
claim_checks.qualification: Fig.4 values are approximate. The attribution to edge conditions is the authors' interpretation. Whether our pedestal-top chord falls in this region must be stated separately.

claim_checks.source_finding: Measured: about 2 ms per frame for curve_fit on a CPU, versus about 210 ns per frame for batched GPU inference on the test set. The authors argue that removing the beam-off wait (up to 1 s) enables continuous measurement. A real-time CES system is stated as a future goal.
claim_checks.allowed_intro_sentence: The authors report sub-microsecond batched offline inference per frame and identify real-time CES as a future goal [Lee2026].
claim_checks.qualification: No online deployment, single-frame latency or report arrival time was measured.

input_target_timing.inputs: Current raw CES spectrum (256 points), one model per channel
input_target_timing.outputs: Δλ and W_D, converted to Ti and vT of C6+
input_target_timing.causal_or_offline: Inference uses the current frame only and needs no future beam-off data. Labels and evaluation are offline.
input_target_timing.reported_vs_physical_truth: Targets are reported modulation-analysis values. The authors note the model inherits their errors and suggest a diagnostic-neutral-beam comparison (p5 Sec.5).

validation.split_unit: Shot-wise 80/10/10 over 321 discharges and 150,890 frames (p3 Sec.3.3)
validation.unknowns: Campaign years; whether the split was chronological. Error bars are the standard deviation of IQR-filtered residuals, not confidence intervals (p4 Sec.3.5).

runtime_or_deployment.what_was_measured: Offline per-frame compute time on CPU (curve fit) and GPU (batched inference)
runtime_or_deployment.what_not_established: Plasma-control-system integration, end-to-end latency, data-arrival timing

forbidden_inferences: NN-CES was deployed in real time
NN-CES was coupled with our nowcaster
edge performance carries over to our chord
faster reading removes or guarantees the need for nowcasting
the model uses BES/ECEI or temporal history
the case-study fidelity in Figs.5-8 represents average performance (authors caution against this, p5)
competing_or_complementary: Complementary. It is an upstream reader that shortens spectrum-to-report processing. Our downstream nowcast estimates the current report before it is available, using past reports plus BES/ECEI. Any combined benefit is untested.
